questions.q: Why does using raw logical reads directly as a reward (e.g. -reads) fail for this project?
options: SQL Server never reports logical reads accurately
Reads range from roughly 50 to 50,000+ across episodes, so wide-range episodes would dominate the training signal
Logical reads cannot be captured via STATISTICS IO
PPO cannot process negative numbers
questions.explain: The huge range in logical reads across narrow vs. wide date ranges means a raw-cost reward would be dominated by whichever episodes happened to be wide-range, drowning out the narrow-range signal.

questions.q: What is the exact reward formula this project uses?
options: reward = -agent_reads
reward = agent_reads / baseline_reads
reward = (baseline_reads - agent_reads) / baseline_reads
reward = baseline_reads - agent_reads
questions.explain: The reward is the baseline's reads minus the agent's reads, divided by the baseline's reads — a scale-invariant ratio.

options: The average logical reads across all past episodes
The logical reads from running the same query with action 0 (no hint), measured once per episode
A hardcoded constant representing an ideal query cost
The logical reads from the slowest hint tried that episode
questions.explain: The baseline is the optimizer's own no-hint plan, measured fresh each episode, so the reward reflects improvement relative to what the optimizer would have done anyway.

questions.q: What reward does the agent receive when it picks action 0 itself?
options: Always +1.0, since it's always a safe choice
Always -1.0, since it never attempts a hint
Exactly 0.0, since agent_reads equals baseline_reads
A random value, since no hint was applied
questions.explain: When the agent picks action 0, its reads equal the baseline reads, making the reward exactly zero — neutral, neither rewarded nor punished.

questions.q: Why is the reward described as 'scale-invariant'?
options: Because it ignores the database schema entirely
Because a relative improvement of the same size produces the same reward value whether the episode involved 50 reads or 50,000 reads
Because it only works for exactly five actions
Because it is always between 0 and 1
questions.explain: Because the reward is a ratio relative to the baseline, episodes of very different absolute magnitude produce comparable rewards for comparable relative improvement.
